sentences.en: Places and people were connected by presences of many kinds.
sentences.zh: 地点与人通过各种各样的存在相互连接。

sentences.en: Places and people were connected by flows of stone, meat and other materials, but were also physically linked by tracks on trails.
sentences.zh: 地点与人通过石头、肉类和其他物质的流动相互连接，但也通过小径上的足迹在物理上联系在一起。

sentences.en: One might even claim that the first revolution imbuing land with social meaning belonged to Neanderthals, not Homo sapiens.
sentences.zh: 有人甚至可能认为，赋予土地社会意义的第一次革命属于尼安德特人，而非智人。

sentences.en: Neanderthals, first kindled history.
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人，最早点燃了历史。

sentences.en: That is from Kindred, a book by Rebecca Rag Sykes that came out last year and which I've been meaning to read ever since it came out.
sentences.zh: 这段话出自丽贝卡·拉格·赛克斯（Rebecca Rag Sykes）去年出版的《亲缘》（Kindred）一书，自出版以来我一直打算阅读。

sentences.en: And I would guess that every five years I will read a book on the subject and every five years I will find that the subject has completely changed.
sentences.zh: 我猜我每五年会读一本关于这个主题的书，而每五年我都会发现这个主题已经完全改变了。

sentences.en: So Becky Rag Sykes' book was the kind of the latest iteration of where thinking is on Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 所以贝基·拉格·赛克斯的书是关于尼安德特人研究现状的最新迭代。

sentences.en: Dominic, are you a fan of Neanderthals or do you?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你是尼安德特人的粉丝吗，还是说你……？

sentences.en: Well, Tom, let me kick off by saying that the last time we had a podcast with a guest, you started with an absolutely, a landmark impersonation, didn't you, of Liam Neeson.
sentences.zh: 嗯，汤姆，让我先说一句，上次我们邀请嘉宾做播客时，你以一段绝对堪称里程碑式的模仿开场，不是吗，模仿的是连姆·尼森（Liam Neeson）。

sentences.en: That's caused a lot of comment.
sentences.zh: 那引起了很多评论。

sentences.en: And I was absolutely bracing myself for you to kick this off with an impersonation of a Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全做好了心理准备，等着你以模仿尼安德特人来开场。

sentences.en: And I think it's a missed opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个错失的机会。

sentences.en: It's a sad moment for the podcast, but we'll just have to fight our way back and hope to win over the listeners some other way.
sentences.zh: 这对播客来说是一个悲伤的时刻，但我们只能努力扭转局面，希望以其他方式赢得听众。

sentences.en: Maybe by the erudition of our gueSt.
sentences.zh: 也许是通过我们嘉宾的博学。

sentences.en: But no, I do know nothing about Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，我对尼安德特人一无所知。

sentences.en: The only thing I know about them really is a massive recommendation to the listeners.
sentences.zh: 我唯一真正了解的是向听众强烈推荐一本书。

sentences.en: William Golding's novel, The Inheritors, which I'm poised to learn is probably all completely wrong, but is an absolutely magnificent novel.
sentences.zh: 威廉·戈尔丁（William Golding）的小说《继承者》（The Inheritors），我正准备去了解它可能完全是错误的，但它绝对是一部宏伟的小说。

sentences.en: If you if you if you've never read any Golding books, for me, it's probably the beSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你从未读过戈尔丁的任何书，对我来说，这可能是最好的一本。

sentences.en: But we can talk about it maybe later in the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们也许可以在播客稍后讨论它。

sentences.en: Well, so the question of how one would impersonate a Neanderthal, did they talk?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于如何模仿尼安德特人的问题，他们会说话吗？

sentences.en: What did they sound like?
sentences.zh: 他们的声音是什么样的？

sentences.en: I mean, this is just one of the many topics that I'm hoping that our guest, Professor Chris Stringer,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是我希望我们的嘉宾克里斯·斯特林格（Chris Stringer）教授能解答的众多话题之一，

sentences.en: who is research leader in human evolution at the Natural History Museum and an absolute hero of mine.
sentences.zh: 他是自然历史博物馆人类进化研究的负责人，也是我绝对的偶像。

sentences.en: Um, he incredibly kindly showed me around the the display on human evolution, the Natural History Museum.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他非常友善地带我参观了自然历史博物馆的人类进化展览。

sentences.en: I remember being given his wonderful book, Homo Britannicus by my parents one Christmas.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一年圣诞节，父母送了我他那本精彩的《不列颠智人》（Homo Britannicus）。

sentences.en: Um, he's got other origin of our species Britain a million years of human story, our human story, you get the drift.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他还有其他著作，比如《我们物种的起源》、《不列颠：一百万年的人类故事》、《我们的人类故事》，你懂我的意思。

sentences.en: The person to ask about human evolution and particularly about the Neanderthals is Chris Stringer, who is joining us.
sentences.zh: 询问人类进化，特别是关于尼安德特人问题的最佳人选就是克里斯·斯特林格，他现在加入了我们。

sentences.en: Chris, thanks so much for coming on.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，非常感谢你能来。

sentences.en: And am I right that that you, like me, did a project on the Neanderthals at primary school?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，你和我一样，在小学时也做过关于尼安德特人的课题吧？

sentences.en: But unlike me, you then went on to become an absolute world expert on it.
sentences.zh: 但与我不同的是，你后来成为了这方面的绝对世界级专家。

sentences.en: So thanks so much for coming on.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢你能来。

sentences.en: Yes, that is in fact right.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实上确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes, I did a project on the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实做过关于尼安德特人的课题。

sentences.en: I think I was nine years old.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时九岁。

sentences.en: I was inspired by BBC radio broadcasts on the prehistory to do that project.
sentences.zh: 我是受到BBC关于史前史的广播节目的启发才做那个课题的。

sentences.en: I had drawings of skulls in there and so on.
sentences.zh: 我在里面画了头骨等等。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, I haven't got it anymore.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我手里已经没有它了。

sentences.en: It's a great shade.
sentences.zh: 真是太可惜了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it was the beginning of something and I couldn't have dreamt I would end up working on this for a career.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但那是一切的开始，我做梦也没想到我最终会把这个作为职业。

sentences.en: So Chris, for people who are approaching this sort of completely blind, when are we talking about Neanderthals?
sentences.zh: 那么克里斯，对于那些完全不了解的人，我们谈论的尼安德特人是什么时候的？

sentences.en: When and what were they?
sentences.zh: 他们是什么时候出现的，又是什么？

sentences.en: Okay, yes.
sentences.zh: 好的，是的。

sentences.en: So in fact, Neanderthals and us are relatively late in the whole story of human evolution.
sentences.zh: 事实上，尼安德特人和我们在整个人类进化史上都算是比较晚近的。

sentences.en: So we think human evolution stretched back at least 7 million years.
sentences.zh: 我们认为人类进化至少可以追溯到700万年前。

sentences.en: And we and the Neanderthals are part of the last few hundred thousand years of that story.
sentences.zh: 而我们和尼安德特人只是这段故事中最后几十万年的一部分。

sentences.en: So we and the Neanderthals are relative latecomers.
sentences.zh: 所以我们和尼安德特人都是相对的后来者。

sentences.en: And the Neanderthal story really begins in the 1850s with the discovery in the Neander Valley of a skeleton,
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人的故事真正始于19世纪50年代，当时在尼安德河谷发现了一具骨架，

sentences.en: a human skeleton that gave its name to the group, Neander Valley and Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 一具赋予了这个群体名字的人类骨架，尼安德河谷和尼安德特人。

sentences.en: So that's a German.
sentences.zh: 所以那是德国人。

sentences.en: He was a German.
sentences.zh: 他是个德国人。

sentences.en: It was found in Germany near Düsseldorf in a valley.
sentences.zh: 它是在德国杜塞尔多夫附近的一个山谷里发现的。

sentences.en: It was actually found during quarrying.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是在采石过程中被发现的。

sentences.en: And it was lucky in a way it was recovered at all.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，它能被找回来真是幸运。

sentences.en: I mean, the workers threw a lot of the bones out of a cave.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，工人们把洞穴里的很多骨头都扔掉了。

sentences.en: And luckily, they were spotted and identified as a strange, as human, but a different kind of human.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，它们被发现并被鉴定为一种奇怪的、人类的，但属于不同种类的人类。

sentences.en: And in 1864, William King, then working in Galway in Ireland, he named this a new species of human, Homo Neanderthalensis.
sentences.zh: 1864年，当时在爱尔兰戈尔韦工作的威廉·金（William King）将其命名为一个新的人类物种：尼安德特人（Homo Neanderthalensis）。

sentences.en: And in fact, there had been two Neanderthal finds before that that had not been recognized up to then.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在此之前还有两次尼安德特人的发现，但当时并没有被识别出来。

sentences.en: So in 1830, a Neanderthal child skull had been found at Ongis in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 1830年，在比利时的昂吉斯（Ongis）发现了一个尼安德特儿童头骨。

sentences.en: And that took another hundred years to be recognized as Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 那又过了一百年才被确认为尼安德特人。

sentences.en: And a skull had been found in Gibraltar in 1848, blasted out of Forbes Quarry.
sentences.zh: 1848年，在直布罗陀的福布斯采石场（Forbes Quarry）炸出了一具头骨。

sentences.en: And that sat on a museum shelf in Gibraltar for many years.
sentences.zh: 那具头骨在直布罗陀的博物馆架子上放了很多年。

sentences.en: So it was the Neanderthal valley find that kind of got the glory and gave its name to the group.
sentences.zh: 所以是尼安德河谷的发现获得了荣誉，并赋予了这个群体名字。

sentences.en: Oh, but so Gibraltar, so actually it's British.
sentences.zh: 哦，但是直布罗陀，所以实际上它是英国的？

sentences.en: Well, you could.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以……

sentences.en: Yes, you could make that claim.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以那样主张。

sentences.en: Or Belgian.
sentences.zh: 或者是比利时的。

sentences.en: Or Belgian.
sentences.zh: 或者是比利时的。

sentences.en: Or Belgian.
sentences.zh: 或者是比利时的。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Am I right that the name is kind of given and announced in 1859, which is the same year as The Origin of Species is published?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，这个名字是在1859年宣布的，也就是《物种起源》出版的那一年？

sentences.en: Well, there were descriptions of the skeleton before that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那之前已经有对骨架的描述了。

sentences.en: But we know that the Gibraltar skull actually was seen by Charles Darwin.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道直布罗陀的头骨实际上被查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin）看过。

sentences.en: Oh, was it?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: After he'd written Origin of Species, but he was shown the skull a couple of years later, the Gibraltar skull.
sentences.zh: 在他写完《物种起源》之后，几年后有人给他看了那具头骨，直布罗陀头骨。

sentences.en: And of course, Darwin was aware of the find from the Neanderthal valley.
sentences.zh: 当然，达尔文也知道尼安德河谷的发现。

sentences.en: And it was the naming in 1864 that obviously started this debate about who these people were.
sentences.zh: 正是1864年的命名显然引发了关于这些人是谁的争论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Were there different species?
sentences.zh: 他们是不同的物种吗？

sentences.en: Were they some kind of version of modern humans?
sentences.zh: 他们是现代人类的某种版本吗？

sentences.en: So there was a debate straight away.
sentences.zh: 所以争论立刻就出现了。

sentences.en: Some people even thought the remains from Neanderthal valley were pathological, that this was some sort of diseased modern human.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至认为尼安德河谷的遗骸是病理性的，认为这是一种患病的现代人类。

sentences.en: It's a Cossack, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 是个哥萨克人，对吧？

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: There was a very extreme view that this was some Cossack soldier, a horseman, and he'd been wounded in battle.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种非常极端的观点，认为这是一个哥萨克士兵，一个骑兵，他在战斗中受了伤。

sentences.en: And he crawled into a cave in Germany and he died there.
sentences.zh: 他爬进德国的一个洞穴，然后死在那里。

sentences.en: And the agony of his pain in the last few days led to these brow ridges developing on his head.
sentences.zh: 他最后几天痛苦的折磨导致他头上长出了这些眉脊。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: So after the Napoleonic Wars or something.
sentences.zh: 所以是在拿破仑战争之后之类的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So he would be a victim of a Cossack from the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 所以他会是拿破仑战争中哥萨克人的受害者。

sentences.en: So, yes, there were some pretty extreme views around and gradually it was recognised that, you know, the Neanderthal Huxley recognised that the Neanderthal skeleton, the skullcap,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，当时有一些相当极端的观点，但逐渐人们认识到，你知道，赫胥黎（Huxley）认识到尼安德特人的骨架，那个头盖骨，

sentences.en: had a big brain as big as a modern human.
sentences.zh: 有着和现代人一样大的大脑。

sentences.en: So that was recognised early on.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点很早就被认可了。

sentences.en: But, of course, the bones of the skeleton were slightly differently shaped from our own.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，骨架的骨头形状与我们略有不同。

sentences.en: And there was this big brow ridge over the eyes, which was obviously quite distinctive.
sentences.zh: 而且眼睛上方有巨大的眉脊，这显然非常独特。

sentences.en: So before this, Chris, did people have any conception that there would have been human relatives, as it were?
sentences.zh: 那么在此之前，克里斯，人们是否意识到会有所谓的人类亲属存在？

sentences.en: Or was this an absolute kind of bolt from the blue?
sentences.zh: 还是说这完全是晴天霹雳？

sentences.en: It was a bolt from the blue.
sentences.zh: 这确实是晴天霹雳。

sentences.en: It was the first ancient kind of human recognised.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个被认可的古代人类。

sentences.en: So fossil human skeletons had been found earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以更早之前也发现过人类化石骨架。

sentences.en: So there was one from Pavilland Cave in Wales, found in the 1820s.
sentences.zh: 比如19世纪20年代在威尔士帕维兰洞穴（Pavilland Cave）发现的一具。

sentences.en: But that was a modern human.
sentences.zh: 但那是现代人类。

sentences.en: So although there was debate about it being prehistoric, in fact, the general view was that it might be even just a Roman age skeleton and not very ancient.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管关于它是否属于史前时期存在争议，但事实上，普遍观点认为它可能只是罗马时代的骨架，并不古老。

sentences.en: So people had very little conception of how deep human history would end up going.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对人类历史到底能追溯到多远几乎没有概念。

sentences.en: There were still, of course, some people working on biblical timescales of just a few thousand years for the whole story.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时仍有一些人坚持圣经的时间尺度，认为整个故事只有几千年。

sentences.en: But, of course, geologists like Charles Lyell were arguing that actually, you know, the Earth history went back millions of years.
sentences.zh: 但当然，像查尔斯·莱尔（Charles Lyell）这样的地质学家在争辩说，实际上，你知道，地球历史可以追溯到数百万年前。

sentences.en: And so some people did speculate that humans could go back a long way.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人确实推测人类可以追溯到很久以前。

sentences.en: But it was the Neanderthal skeleton that really started this debate about ancient humans that were potentially different from us.
sentences.zh: 但正是尼安德特人的骨架真正开启了关于可能与我们不同的古代人类的争论。

sentences.en: Chris, in The Origin of Species, Darwin famously does not talk about human evolution.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，在《物种起源》中，达尔文著名地没有谈论人类进化。

sentences.en: And he does then go on in The Sentent of Man to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他后来在《人类的由来》（The Descent of Man）中谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: How unsettling is the discovery of Neanderthals to human conceptions of themselves?
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人的发现对人类的自我认知有多大的冲击？

sentences.en: And how does it kind of feed through into, I don't know, kind of ideas of scientific racism, hierarchy of races and things like that,
sentences.zh: 它又是如何影响到，我不知道，某种科学种族主义、种族等级制度之类的思想，

sentences.en: that really kind of takes off after The Origin of Species?
sentences.zh: 这些思想在《物种起源》之后确实开始流行起来？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, of course, it does get drawn into that debate.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，它确实被卷入了那场争论。

sentences.en: So, Huxley, recognising that this was large-brained, he, in a sense, saw the Neanderthal skeleton, or the skull in particular, as being one end of a long chain of humans that was,
sentences.zh: 所以，赫胥黎认识到这是一个大脑袋的人类，他在某种意义上将尼安德特人骨架，特别是头骨，视为人类长链的一端，

sentences.en: you know, Neanderthal with very large brow ridges at one end.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一端是眉脊非常大的尼安德特人。

sentences.en: And then moving through, you know, some more recent human finds, and there were more recent human finds that had bigger brow ridges than others.
sentences.zh: 然后过渡到，你知道，一些更近期的发现，确实有一些比其他人眉脊更大的近期人类发现。

sentences.en: So, for Huxley, this was one end of a long chain of humanity.
sentences.zh: 所以对赫胥黎来说，这是人类长链的一端。

sentences.en: So, I suppose, you know, he would have argued it could even be an extreme form of Homo sapiens, their own species.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道，他会争辩说它甚至可能是智人的一种极端形式，也就是他们自己的物种。

sentences.en: But then there were other people, as I say, who named it as a distinct species.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，还有其他人将其命名为一个独特的物种。

sentences.en: William King described, you know, really quite a lot of very primitive and you could say bestial features on this Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 威廉·金描述了，你知道，在这个尼安德特人身上确实有相当多非常原始，甚至可以说野蛮的特征。

sentences.en: So, straight away, there was a debate there about, was this just a different kind of modern human, or could it be something really different,
sentences.zh: 所以，立刻就出现了一场争论，这只是不同种类的现代人，还是可能是真正不同的东西，

sentences.en: and with the ideas of evolution much more primitive.
sentences.zh: 而且随着进化论思想，它显得更加原始。

sentences.en: And by the time we get to the 1900s, of course, no really ancient fossils have been found in places like Africa.
sentences.zh: 到了1900年代，当然，在非洲等地还没有发现真正古老的化石。

sentences.en: So, the African fossil discoveries that we know about now, those only started to appear in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在所知的非洲化石发现，直到1920年代才开始出现。

sentences.en: So, in the early 1900s, people were looking for kind of so-called missing links.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1900年代初期，人们正在寻找所谓的缺失环节。

sentences.en: And there had been a find in Java that we now know is a Homo erectus, and that was really quite ape-like.
sentences.zh: 爪哇曾有一个发现，我们现在知道那是直立人（Homo erectus），它确实非常像猿。

sentences.en: And the Neanderthals were also in that debate, and some of the reconstructions of Neanderthals made them very ape-like.
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人也参与了那场争论，一些对尼安德特人的复原图使他们看起来非常像猿。

sentences.en: They were depicted as being bent-kneed, grasping big toes, very hairy, head hung forward, not walking fully erect.
sentences.zh: 他们被描绘成膝盖弯曲、脚趾抓握、毛发浓密、头部前倾，不能完全直立行走。

sentences.en: So, there was that debate going on about them being really an ape-like form of human, a sort of missing link.
sentences.zh: 所以当时关于他们是真正像猿的人类形式，即某种缺失环节的争论一直在进行。

sentences.en: Whereas, you know, now, of course, the debate about Neanderthals has moved on.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，现在关于尼安德特人的争论当然已经向前发展了。

sentences.en: I think it's much more difficult to say the Neanderthals were even culturally inferior to modern humans who were around at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我认为说尼安德特人在文化上甚至不如同时代的现代人要困难得多。

sentences.en: So, the behavioural gap between Neanderthals and us has narrowed.
sentences.zh: 所以，尼安德特人和我们之间的行为差距已经缩小了。

sentences.en: Some people would say it's disappeared.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会说它已经消失了。

sentences.en: And I think there is this risk of, you know, getting them into this debate about inferiority and superiority.
sentences.zh: 我认为存在这种风险，你知道，把他们卷入关于优劣的争论中。

sentences.en: And it's part of this misconception that, you know, all these human forms were evolving towards us,
sentences.zh: 这是误解的一部分，你知道，所有这些人类形式都在向我们进化，

sentences.en: that we were some kind of perfection of humanity, and everything was evolving to be like us.
sentences.zh: 我们是某种人类的完美形态，一切都在进化得像我们一样。

sentences.en: And if they evolved to be like us, they were successful.
sentences.zh: 如果他们进化得像我们，他们就是成功的。

sentences.en: And if they didn't evolve to be like us, they were unsuccessful.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没有进化得像我们，他们就是不成功的。

sentences.en: So, there is that debate as well.
sentences.zh: 所以也存在那种争论。

sentences.en: And, yes, it does link into this idea of superiority, you know, modernity.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，它确实与这种优越感、你知道，现代性的观念联系在一起。

sentences.en: You know, the fact that we're so numerous around the world and apparently so successful means that some people see us as the kind of height of evolution.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在世界各地数量如此之多，而且看起来如此成功，这意味着有些人视我们为进化的巅峰。

sentences.en: Whereas, you know, I'm a paleontologist in the paleontology department, and I, you know, I see us as just another form of animal in a sense.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，我是古生物学系的古生物学家，我，你知道，从某种意义上说，我视我们为另一种形式的动物。

sentences.en: We're very successful in numbers, but whether we're successful in the long term, we're newcomers in evolution.
sentences.zh: 我们在数量上非常成功，但我们是否在长期内成功，我们只是进化中的后来者。

sentences.en: Could you not then, though, say that we clearly were more successful than Neanderthals, as evidenced by the fact that there are an awful lot of us and there are none of them?
sentences.zh: 难道你不能说我们显然比尼安德特人更成功吗，证据就是我们有很多人，而他们一个都没有？

sentences.en: I mean, would that be too simplistic a way of putting it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这样说会不会太简单化了？

sentences.en: Well, it's one way of measuring success.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是衡量成功的一种方式。

sentences.en: But if you were measuring success in terms of numbers, then things like bacteria or other forms of life would be more successful than us.
sentences.zh: 但如果你用数字来衡量成功，那么像细菌或其他生命形式就会比我们更成功。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And obviously, you know, if we look at the way our planet is and the health of our planet at the moment, you could see that our success might seem great.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，如果你看看我们星球现在的状况以及它的健康程度，你可能会觉得我们的成功似乎很了不起。

sentences.en: But, you know, how successful we will look in a few thousand years is another story.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，几千年后我们看起来是否还那么成功，那就是另一回事了。

sentences.en: So in geological time, as I say, we and the Neanderthals are newcomers to the story.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我所说，在地质时间尺度上，我们和尼安德特人都是这个故事里的新来者。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, Homo erectus on conventional views, that species of human lasted for at least one and a half million years.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，按照传统观点，直立人那种人类物种至少存活了一百五十万年。

sentences.en: So we've got a long way to go to match that in terms of longevity.
sentences.zh: 所以就寿命而言，我们还有很长的路要走才能与之相比。

sentences.en: So I think it depends what you measure by success.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这取决于你如何定义成功。

sentences.en: Is it just about numbers?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是关于数量吗？

sentences.en: It's also about your effect on the environment, how successful you are in the long term.
sentences.zh: 这还关乎你对环境的影响，以及你从长远来看有多成功。

sentences.en: And I think there's certainly doubts about how successful we're going to be in the long term as a species.
sentences.zh: 我认为，作为一个物种，我们从长远来看是否会成功，这无疑是令人怀疑的。

sentences.en: Well, so, Chris, picking up on that, one of the reasons why I quoted Becky Ragsykes's wonderful book with that thing, Neanderthals First Kindled History.
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯，接着这一点说，我引用贝基·拉格赛克斯那本精彩著作《尼安德特人点燃了历史》的原因之一就是这个。

sentences.en: So this is a history podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个历史播客。

sentences.en: Does it make sense to think of Neanderthals as offering us as Homo sapiens a kind of an alternative sense of how history might have evolved?
sentences.zh: 把尼安德特人视为为我们智人提供了一种历史演变可能性的替代视角，这合理吗？

sentences.en: Because you're basically saying that Neanderthals and Homo sapiens constitute kind of two divergent ways of being human.
sentences.zh: 因为你基本上是在说，尼安德特人和智人构成了两种不同的人类生存方式。

sentences.en: And if we if we have history and it's made up of how we interact with one another, how we interact with the environment,
sentences.zh: 如果我们拥有历史，而历史是由我们彼此之间的互动、我们与环境的互动所构成的，

sentences.en: how we've kind of developed a culture over the course of the millennia.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何在几千年的时间里发展出一种文化。

sentences.en: Can we say the same about Neanderthals?
sentences.zh: 我们能对尼安德特人说同样的话吗？

sentences.en: Did Neanderthals also construct something that we would recognise as a kind of historical culture, perhaps?
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人是否也构建了我们可能认可的那种历史文化？

sentences.en: I think it depends how you define history and culture.
sentences.zh: 我认为这取决于你如何定义历史和文化。

sentences.en: I think that obviously these people were surviving at the time with with a culture.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，这些人当时就是带着文化生存下来的。

sentences.en: They had a whole suite of features and behaviours that they passed on through time.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有一整套随时间传承下来的特征和行为。

sentences.en: So in a sense, they were creating history in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，他们确实在以那种方式创造历史。

sentences.en: They probably did tell stories and pass them down.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能讲述过故事并代代相传。

sentences.en: They probably had language.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能拥有语言。

sentences.en: Modern humans did, too.
sentences.zh: 现代人类也是如此。

sentences.en: And it's not just about even us and Neanderthals, because we know there was another kind of human over in East Asia called the Denisovans.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅关乎我们和尼安德特人，因为我们知道在东亚还有另一种人类，叫做丹尼索瓦人。

sentences.en: And they're a third kind of human.
sentences.zh: 他们是第三种人类。

sentences.en: And in fact, looking more widely in the last 100,000 years, there were at least five kinds of humans around on the Earth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，放眼过去十万年，地球上至少存在过五种人类。

sentences.en: So it's not even just us and Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 所以这甚至不仅仅是我们和尼安德特人的问题。

sentences.en: There were all these different experiments in how to be a human.
sentences.zh: 当时有各种各样的关于如何成为人类的实验。

sentences.en: So we're the one that survived.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是唯一幸存下来的那一种。

sentences.en: The others disappeared.
sentences.zh: 其他的都消失了。

sentences.en: And obviously, one of the big questions is, why are we the only ones left of all these experiments to be human?
sentences.zh: 显而易见，最大的问题之一是，为什么在所有这些成为人类的实验中，只有我们留了下来？

sentences.en: As a complete outsider, can I ask a quick definitional question?
sentences.zh: 作为一个完全的外行，我可以问一个简单的定义问题吗？

sentences.en: So we and Neanderthals and Denisovans, for example, are all human.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们、尼安德特人和丹尼索瓦人都是人类。

sentences.en: But what is a human?
sentences.zh: 但什么是人类？

sentences.en: Is it just a particular kind of ape?
sentences.zh: 它只是某种特定的猿类吗？

sentences.en: Or what is the definition?
sentences.zh: 或者说定义是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: And there isn't agreement on experts.
sentences.zh: 专家们对此并没有达成共识。

sentences.en: So for me, the genus Homo, so we're Homo sapiens, the Neanderthals, I call them Homo Neanderthalensis.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，人属，也就是我们智人，还有尼安德特人，我称他们为尼安德特人种。

sentences.en: Membership of the genus Homo, for me, is what is being human.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，成为人属的成员就是人类的定义。

sentences.en: And being in that genus, the representatives have larger brains.
sentences.zh: 作为该属的代表，他们拥有更大的大脑。

sentences.en: They have a human-shaped body.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有人类形状的身体。

sentences.en: They have technology.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有技术。

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: So there are certain features in the skeleton that we can pick up in fossils to determine whether something's human or not.
sentences.zh: 所以骨骼中确实存在某些特征，我们可以通过化石来判断某物是否属于人类。

sentences.en: Now, for some people, human is a term they would only apply to Homo sapiens, our own species.
sentences.zh: 现在，对一些人来说，人类这个词只适用于智人，也就是我们自己的物种。

sentences.en: I find that a bit worrying because it means Neanderthals aren't human.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点令人担忧，因为这意味着尼安德特人不是人类。

sentences.en: And as we're going to come on to discuss, no doubt, we have interbred with the Neanderthals and with the Denisovans.
sentences.zh: 而且正如我们接下来要讨论的，毫无疑问，我们曾与尼安德特人和丹尼索瓦人杂交过。

sentences.en: So in a sense, that means we, as humans, we interbred with non-humans.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这意味着我们作为人类，曾与非人类杂交。

sentences.en: I think that's really pushing the arguments in a strange direction.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实把论点推向了一个奇怪的方向。

sentences.en: So for me, membership of the genus Homo means human.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，人属的成员就是人类。

sentences.en: So yes, we, Neanderthals, are Homo, so we are human.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我们和尼安德特人都属于人属，所以我们都是人类。

sentences.en: So I just see them, as you say, as another model of human, another way to be human.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是像你所说的那样，把他们看作人类的另一种模式，另一种成为人类的方式。

sentences.en: In a sense, maybe we got lucky.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，也许我们比较幸运。

sentences.en: That could be why we're here and they're not.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么我们还在这里，而他们不在了。

sentences.en: We just got lucky.
sentences.zh: 我们只是运气好。

sentences.en: Certainly, certain things happened in our prehistory that helped us survive.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们的史前时期确实发生了一些事情，帮助我们生存了下来。

sentences.en: And in the Neanderthals' case, things turned against them.
sentences.zh: 而在尼安德特人的案例中，情况对他们不利。

sentences.en: But we should bear in mind with all of this that they're not completely gone.
sentences.zh: 但我们应该记住，他们并没有完全消失。

sentences.en: And of course, we'll come on to this.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But yes, they're physically extinct and may have gone extinct around 40,000 years ago physically.
sentences.zh: 但确实，他们在物理上已经灭绝了，可能在大约四万年前就在物理上灭绝了。

sentences.en: But they live on in our DNA.
sentences.zh: 但他们活在我们的DNA里。

sentences.en: So, you know, each of us now in this podcast have Neanderthal DNA around the level of probably 2%.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们播客里的每个人现在都有大约2%的尼安德特人DNA。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, you know, we've all got a bit of Neanderthal in our DNA.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们每个人的DNA里都有点尼安德特人的成分。

sentences.en: And that's true for the majority of people in the world today.
sentences.zh: 这对当今世界上大多数人来说都是事实。

sentences.en: So the Neanderthals have not disappeared completely.
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人并没有完全消失。

sentences.en: And neither have the Denisovans.
sentences.zh: 丹尼索瓦人也没有。

sentences.en: Their DNA lives on in billions of people today as well.
sentences.zh: 他们的DNA今天也活在数十亿人的体内。

sentences.en: The way that Neanderthals have been understood since they were first discovered.
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人自被发现以来，人们对他们的理解方式发生了变化。

sentences.en: So, as you said, to begin with, they're kind of cast as savage, brutish, ape-like.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，起初他们被描绘成野蛮、粗鲁、像猿类一样。

sentences.en: And then, am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: I mean, for instance, in William Golding's book that Dominic mentioned, The Inheritors,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，例如，多米尼克提到的威廉·戈尔丁的书《继承者》，

sentences.en: The Inheritors are Homo sapiens.
sentences.zh: 《继承者》里的主角是智人。

sentences.en: And we see the world through Neanderthal eyes.
sentences.zh: 我们通过尼安德特人的眼睛看世界。

sentences.en: And I mean, I'm guessing I don't know enough about the book, actually, but I'm guessing that it's kind of influenced by decolonization, the idea that kind of anxiety about Western
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜——其实我对这本书了解不够——但我猜它受到了非殖民化的影响，那种对西方殖民主义的焦虑感，也许吧。

sentences.en: colonialism, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是戈尔丁对人类邪恶的感知，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.zh: 你读过《蝇王》之类的书吧。

sentences.zh: 那是尼安德特人考古学的伟大遗址之一，发现了一具尸体，一具尼安德特人的尸体，看起来像是一个墓葬。

sentences.zh: 据我所知，现在人们不再认为那是真的了。

sentences.en: not as brutish and thuggish, but kind of peace loving, wiped out by the sinister intrusion of

sentences.zh: 据推测，如果他们进行了杂交，那么并不一定是一方在捕食另一方，他们可能是有过某种互动。

sentences.en: And now have we moved on from that to a position where we're saying that, you know, what were the relations between Homo sapiens and Neanderthals?
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，如果我们能回到那个特定的问题，

sentences.en: and I'm going to go back in time about this whole question of the image of the Neanderthals firSt.
