sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们转向了60年代的沙尼达尔。

sentences.en: It's the other side of the mirror.
sentences.zh: 是的，拉尔夫·塞莱基，他领导了沙尼达尔的挖掘工作，写了一本书叫《尼安德特人》，

sentences.en: And as you say, they're moving on to the 1960s with Shanidar.
sentences.zh: 我想书名是《第一批花之子》，或者《第一朵花》，这非常符合那个时代。

sentences.en: Yes, Ralph Selecki, who led the excavations at Shanidar, wrote a book called Neanderthals,
sentences.zh: 所以是的，钟摆来回摆动。

sentences.en: the first flower children, I think it was called, or the first flower, very much a book of its time.
sentences.zh: 让我们进入90年代。

sentences.en: And yes, so the pendulum has swung backwards and forwards.
sentences.zh: 我认为钟摆已经远离了那种尼安德特人的形象，转而强调他们的独特性。

sentences.en: Let's say we go on to the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是在非洲进化的。

sentences.en: I think the pendulum had swung away from that image of the Neanderthals to make them more distinct.
sentences.zh: 非洲的环境一定有什么东西赋予了我们优势。

sentences.en: You know, we had evolved in Africa.
sentences.zh: 也许我们发展出了洞穴艺术，发展出了复杂的工具。

sentences.en: And there must be something about the African environment that gave us superiority.
sentences.zh: 这使我们在非洲表现出色，然后走出非洲，并很快取代了尼安德特人。

sentences.en: Maybe we developed cave art and we developed sophisticated tools.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是90年代的主流观点。

sentences.en: And that led us to do well in Africa and then come out of Africa and then very quickly replace the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们进入2000年代，随着越来越多的发现被挖掘出来，我们开始看到钟摆再次摆回，

sentences.en: And so that was the view maybe in the 1990s, the predominant view.
sentences.zh: 这些发现表明，尼安德特人在十万或二十万年前的行为复杂性上与现代人类相当。

sentences.en: But then as we get into the 2000s, we start to see the pendulum swing back again as more and more discoveries are made,
sentences.zh: 而且这些发现还在不断涌现。

sentences.en: which show that the Neanderthals were matching modern humans, let's say, 100,000 or 200,000 years ago in their complexity of behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，正如我所说，如果说存在行为差距，那也是非常微小的。

sentences.en: And those discoveries are still coming through.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可能应该把尼安德特人看作是他们自己行为方式上的成功者。

sentences.en: And so now, as I say, if there is a behavioral gap, it's a very narrow one.
sentences.zh: 而我们在自己的行为方式上也是成功的。

sentences.en: And I think probably we should look at the Neanderthals as being very successful in their own right in what they did.
sentences.zh: 我们与他们分享了许多行为，但也有一些区别。

sentences.en: And we were successful in our own right in what we did.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的生存，你知道，

sentences.en: We shared many behaviors with them, but there were some distinctions.
sentences.zh: 可能既是运气问题，也可能是因为我们在正确的时间、正确的地点，拥有了赋予我们成功的那一点点行为特征。

sentences.en: And I think that our survival, you know,
sentences.zh: 最终可能甚至归结为数量问题，因为尼安德特人生活在一个气候反复发生剧烈变化的环境中。

sentences.en: probably was a matter of luck as well as perhaps being in the right place and the right time with the right little bits of behavior that gave us success.
sentences.zh: 每隔几千年，欧洲的气候就会从接近现代的温暖切换到严寒。

sentences.en: And it may have even been down to numbers in the end that the Neanderthals had been living in an environment where there were very severe climate changes happening repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 这些变化发生得非常迅速，每隔几百年或几千年就会发生一次。

sentences.en: Every few thousand years, the climate in Europe switched back from nearly as warm as the present day to bitterly cold.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为尼安德特人在这种情况下永远无法增加他们的人口数量。

sentences.en: These changes happened very rapidly and they happened every few hundred or few thousand years.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的多样性、他们的人数减少了。

sentences.en: So I think the Neanderthals were never able to build up their numbers under those circumstances.
sentences.zh: 他们的遗传多样性很低。

sentences.en: So their diversity, their numbers were reduced.
sentences.zh: 他们的人数很少。

sentences.en: They had low genetic diversity.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，也许他们已经是一个受威胁的物种了。

sentences.en: They had low numbers.
sentences.zh: 然后现代人类在大约六万年前走出非洲，开始进入尼安德特人的领地。

sentences.en: And so in a sense, maybe they were already a threatened species.
sentences.zh: 这可能最终导致他们极度不稳定，以至于他们灭绝了。

sentences.en: And then modern humans came out of Africa about 60,000 years ago, started entering the territory of the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着你几乎可以画一张地图？

sentences.en: And that may have eventually just destabilized them so much that they just went extinct.
sentences.zh: 汤姆刚才在谈论历史。

sentences.en: Does that mean you could almost draw a map?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们不仅仅通过故事来理解历史。

sentences.en: Tom was talking about history.
sentences.zh: 这通过插图和地图来理解历史。

sentences.en: And, you know, we don't just make sense of history through stories.
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着你几乎可以画一张地图，然后说这些部分是人类居住的，或者抱歉，是现代人类，也就是智人居住的？

sentences.en: This makes sense of history through illustrations and maps.
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着你几乎可以画一张地图，然后说这些部分是人类居住的，或者抱歉，是现代人类，也就是智人居住的？

sentences.en: Does that mean you could almost draw a map and you could say this these bits are kind of human inhabited or sorry, modern human kind of homo sapiens inhabited.
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着你几乎可以画一张地图，然后说这些部分是人类居住的，或者抱歉，是现代人类，也就是智人居住的？

sentences.en: And these bits are kind of Neanderthal territory or something.
sentences.zh: 这些碎片基本上属于尼安德特人的地盘，或者类似的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, because you're suggesting that they're in different places, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为你暗示它们基本上位于不同的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we don't have the data to put them on the map at the same time in the same places, except in a couple of places.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以除了少数几个地方，我们没有数据能把它们同时放在地图上的同一地点。

sentences.en: So broadly speaking, the Neanderthals were in occupation of Europe from their lineage, at least from more than 400,000 years ago down to about 40,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以从广义上讲，尼安德特人从他们的血统起源开始，至少从40多万年前一直到大约4万年前，一直占据着欧洲。

sentences.en: So most of the fossils we find are Neanderthal in that time zone.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在那个时间段发现的大多数化石都是尼安德特人的。

sentences.en: But there are a few exceptions.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些例外。

sentences.en: So there is a fossil from Greece that I was involved in studying from a site called Epidema in the Peloponnese.
sentences.zh: 比如，希腊有一个化石，我曾参与研究，来自伯罗奔尼撒半岛一个叫埃皮迪马（Epidema）的遗址。

sentences.en: And that cave site has what seems to be a homo sapiens fossil over 200,000 years old and then after it, a Neanderthal fossil.
sentences.zh: 那个洞穴遗址里似乎有一个20多万年前的智人化石，而在它之后，又有一个尼安德特人化石。

sentences.en: So there we've got what may be a brief appearance of modern humans or at least homo sapiens over 200,000 years ago in the eastern Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在那里发现了现代人类，或者至少是智人，在20多万年前的地中海东部可能出现过短暂的踪迹。

sentences.en: But then it goes again.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们又消失了。

sentences.en: And then we come on to the period between 40,000 and 50,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 接着我们来到4万到5万年前的时期。

sentences.en: And it looks like we have kind of a similar story that modern humans are kind of appearing in Europe briefly, but then disappearing again.
sentences.zh: 看起来情况类似，现代人类似乎在欧洲短暂出现过，但随后又消失了。

sentences.en: So the Neanderthals remain the main occupants of Europe until about 40,000 years ago when they go extinct.
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人一直保持着欧洲主要居住者的地位，直到大约4万年前他们灭绝为止。

sentences.en: But modern humans are making, if you like, incursions, dispersals into Neanderthal territory.
sentences.zh: 但现代人类正在，如果你愿意这么说的话，对尼安德特人的领地进行入侵和扩散。

sentences.en: And eventually, by about 41,000 years, modern humans are there in sufficiently large numbers that they effectively take over from the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 最终，到了大约4.1万年前，现代人类的数量已经足够多，以至于他们实际上取代了尼安德特人。

sentences.en: And one of the interesting things is, and this is purely speculation because we don't have all the data,
sentences.zh: 其中一个有趣的事情是——这纯属推测，因为我们没有所有数据——

sentences.en: is that we know that a number of those modern humans that were moving into Neanderthal territory over 40,000 years ago,
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在4万多年前进入尼安德特人领地的那些现代人类中，

sentences.en: a number of them show signs of interbreeding with the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 有相当一部分人表现出与尼安德特人通婚的迹象。

sentences.en: And so it's possible that Neanderthal individuals, male or female, were being taken into the modern human groups.
sentences.zh: 所以，尼安德特人个体，无论是男性还是女性，都有可能被现代人类群体吸收了。

sentences.en: Now, if the Neanderthals were fewer in number, they're losing prime age breeding individuals into the modern human groups.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果尼安德特人的数量较少，他们就会失去处于生育黄金期的个体，这些个体流向了现代人类群体。

sentences.en: And that would be one way in which they might have just faded away.
sentences.zh: 这可能是他们逐渐消失的一种方式。

sentences.en: Because if you're taking prime age adults breeding individuals out of a population, that population is not going to be able to sustain itself if that behavior continues.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不断地从一个种群中带走处于生育黄金期的成年个体，如果这种行为持续下去，该种群将无法维持自身繁衍。

sentences.en: So what's odd is that the late Neanderthals we have DNA for don't show evidence of DNA from modern humans.
sentences.zh: 所以奇怪的是，我们拥有DNA的晚期尼安德特人并没有显示出携带现代人类DNA的证据。

sentences.en: So either the interbreeding was mainly going one way into modern human gene pools and Neanderthals being taken out of their own gene pool,
sentences.zh: 所以要么是通婚主要是单向的，即基因流入了现代人类的基因库，而尼安德特人从他们自己的基因库中被带走，

sentences.en: or the interbreeding in the other direction was unsuccessful and those individuals did not survive to breed on.
sentences.zh: 要么是另一个方向的通婚并不成功，那些个体没能存活下来并继续繁衍。

sentences.en: So we're beginning to learn about this interesting phase and how the interbreeding even happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始了解这个有趣的阶段，以及通婚究竟是如何发生的。

sentences.en: We don't really know the details.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正了解细节。

sentences.en: Was it friendly?
sentences.zh: 是友好的吗？

sentences.en: Was it, you know, hostile?
sentences.zh: 是，你知道，敌对的吗？

sentences.en: Capturing females, for example, which does happen sometimes in chimpanzee groups and some hunter-gatherer groups.
sentences.zh: 比如掠夺女性，这在黑猩猩群体和一些狩猎采集群体中确实有时会发生。

sentences.en: Was it adopting orphan babies?
sentences.zh: 是收养孤儿吗？

sentences.en: Those are all possibilities.
sentences.zh: 这些都是可能性。

sentences.en: And indeed, all of those things could have happened at different times in different places.
sentences.zh: 事实上，所有这些事情都可能在不同的时间、不同的地点发生过。

sentences.en: So eventually, we'll have more data to actually reconstruct how these people were interbreeding.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，我们将有更多的数据来真正还原这些人是如何通婚的。

sentences.en: It will be possible one day to tell whether it was the interbreeding of Neanderthals was mainly through females or males.
sentences.zh: 总有一天，我们有可能判断出尼安德特人的通婚主要是通过女性还是男性。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么判断？

sentences.en: How will we possibly, how do we know that?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么可能，我们怎么知道这一点？

sentences.en: Forgive my ignorance.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我的无知。

sentences.en: Well, because of the X and Y chromosomes, for example, that obviously males have an X and a Y chromosome.
sentences.zh: 嗯，以X和Y染色体为例，显然男性拥有一个X染色体和一个Y染色体。

sentences.en: Females have two X chromosomes.
sentences.zh: 女性拥有两个X染色体。

sentences.en: Of course, there are other chromosome mixtures as well, but those are the two main mixtures.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有其他的染色体组合，但这是两种主要的组合。

sentences.en: And so eventually, geneticists will be able to reconstruct, you know, the Neanderthal DNA that's coming in.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，遗传学家将能够重建，你知道，那些进入的尼安德特人DNA。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Could it be mediated through, mainly through females or males?
sentences.zh: 这可能是通过，主要是通过女性还是男性介导的？

sentences.en: So if it was females, that might imply that they were kind of slaves or that they were being kidnapped for breeding purposes, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以如果是女性，那可能意味着她们是某种奴隶，或者她们基本上是为了繁衍目的而被绑架的。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, it's possible.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，这是可能的。

sentences.en: Or it might be even the mating systems of these people meant that the females were mobile and moving into male groups predominantly rather than the other way around.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至可能是这些人的交配系统意味着女性具有流动性，主要是进入男性群体，而不是反过来。

sentences.en: So there could even be social reasons why it might be in that direction.
sentences.zh: 所以甚至可能存在社会原因导致它朝那个方向发展。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's a lot to learn about this time period, and it will be interesting to see how the data unfold on this.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，关于这个时期还有很多东西要学，看看相关数据如何展开将会很有趣。

sentences.en: Chris, we really ought to go for a break.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们真的该休息一下了。

sentences.en: And when we come back, I would love to talk about what we can say about Neanderthal society, presumably societies.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，我很想谈谈关于尼安德特人社会，大概是社会，我们能说些什么。

sentences.en: I'm guessing there were lots of different kinds.
sentences.zh: 我猜想他们有很多不同的类型。

sentences.en: But just on this topic, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但就这个话题而言，我的意思是，

sentences.en: what seems really interesting about the way that Neanderthals have been understood right from the beginning is that they've kind of provided a mirror that is held up to anxieties and assumptions among contemporary societies.
sentences.zh: 关于尼安德特人从一开始就被理解的方式，真正有趣的是，他们提供了一面镜子，映照出当代社会中的焦虑和假设。

sentences.en: And the way that we've understood Neanderthals has kind of evolved as our cultural, political sensibilities have evolved as well.
sentences.zh: 我们理解尼安德特人的方式，也随着我们文化和政治敏感度的演变而演变。

sentences.en: And I'm guessing that at the moment, with all the DNA, with all the kind of scientific study, with all the kind of objectivity that scientists like yourself bring to it,
sentences.zh: 我猜想目前，有了所有的DNA研究，有了所有的科学研究，有了像你这样的科学家所带来的那种客观性，

sentences.en: nevertheless, these are quite politically sensitive areas.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这些领域在政治上仍然相当敏感。

sentences.en: The question of migration, of population replacement, all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 关于移民、人口更替的问题，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Do you think that, you know, just as in the 60s, people were seeing flower power reflected back in burial sites and so on,
sentences.zh: 你认为，你知道，就像在60年代，人们在墓葬遗址中看到了“花的力量”（Flower Power）的反映等等，

sentences.en: do you think now with all the kind of current political anxieties that are roiling Western societies, is that still going on?
sentences.zh: 你认为现在，随着所有这些在西方社会翻腾的当前政治焦虑，这种情况还在发生吗？

sentences.en: In other words, is how we understand Neanderthals and particularly their relationship to Homo sapiens kind of determined by politics as much as by science?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们对尼安德特人的理解，特别是他们与智人的关系，是否像受科学影响一样，也受到政治的左右？

sentences.en: Well, it's certainly coming into it now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在确实涉及到了这一点。

sentences.en: So there are some people who think that even calling the Neanderthals a different species is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人认为，即使称尼安德特人为不同的物种也是危险的。

sentences.en: It's in a sense racist that we're setting up, you know, differences in humanity, which can then be applied to populations today.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是种族主义，因为我们正在建立，你知道，人类之间的差异，而这些差异随后可以应用于今天的人群。

sentences.en: I take a different view because for me, our species, Homo sapiens, we can diagnose it by shared features.
sentences.zh: 我持不同观点，因为对我来说，我们的物种，智人，我们可以通过共享特征来诊断它。

sentences.en: That is how we do it.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样做的。

sentences.en: We look at the shared features of modern humans around the world today.
sentences.zh: 我们观察当今世界各地现代人类的共享特征。

sentences.en: And that's how we can say the Neanderthals are a different species because they don't show those shared features.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们能说尼安德特人是不同物种的原因，因为他们没有表现出那些共享特征。

sentences.en: Equally, geneticists can look at the modern human genome and they can find a suite of features there which are characterized by modern humans around the world,
sentences.zh: 同样，遗传学家可以观察现代人类基因组，他们可以在其中找到一套特征，这些特征是世界各地现代人类的典型特征，

sentences.en: which we don't find in the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 而我们在尼安德特人身上找不到这些特征。

sentences.en: So for me, having Neanderthals as a distinct species doesn't, in a sense, produce racial divisions within modern humans.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，将尼安德特人视为一个独特的物种，在某种意义上并不会在现代人类内部制造种族分裂。

sentences.en: For me, it's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I think what unites us is what unites us as a species compared with the Neanderthals and these earlier human species.
sentences.zh: 我认为将我们团结在一起的，是作为物种的我们，与尼安德特人和这些早期人类物种相比，所共有的东西。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: OK, so we'll take a break now.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们现在休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, maybe we could look at and work out what we know about how Neanderthals lived.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，也许我们可以研究并弄清楚我们对尼安德特人的生活方式了解多少。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: Chris Stringer, Professor Chris Stringer, has been replenishing his energy with some fruit.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·斯特林格（Chris Stringer），克里斯·斯特林格教授，一直在用水果补充能量。

sentences.en: Tom Holland has been honing his Neanderthal impression, which I'm reliably assured he will be doing at the end of this episode.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德（Tom Holland）一直在磨练他的尼安德特人模仿秀，据我可靠保证，他将在本集结束时表演。

sentences.en: And Tom, you had a question for Chris, didn't you, about Neanderthals, what we know of Neanderthals, so both physically and kind of socially.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你有一个关于克里斯的问题，对吧，关于尼安德特人，我们对尼安德特人的了解，无论是生理上还是社会上。

sentences.en: Well, I guess, so Chris, I guess Dominic has laid down this challenge that I have to do with an impression of a Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，克里斯，我想多米尼克已经提出了这个挑战，我必须模仿一个尼安德特人。

sentences.en: Would we have any way of knowing what a Neanderthal sounded like?
sentences.zh: 我们有什么办法知道尼安德特人的声音是什么样的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, presumably they have language.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大概他们有语言。

sentences.en: What can we say about language, how they sounded?
sentences.zh: 关于语言，他们的声音，我们能说些什么？

sentences.en: What do we know about that?
sentences.zh: 我们对此了解多少？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's a question of great interest, and it's one of the most difficult ones to answer, of course.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是一个非常令人感兴趣的问题，当然，这也是最难回答的问题之一。

sentences.en: So some people have tried to reconstruct what a Neanderthal would sound like from the anatomy.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人试图从解剖结构上重建尼安德特人的声音。

sentences.en: And possibly their voice box was not as deeply placed as ours, so they may have actually had a higher-pitched voice.
sentences.zh: 可能他们的喉头位置不像我们那么靠下，所以他们实际上可能拥有更高音调的声音。

sentences.en: Oh, well, there's...
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，有……

sentences.en: I'm looking forward to your reconstruction, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我很期待你的重建，汤姆。

sentences.en: If you search on the BBC website, you'll find a very amusing reconstruction there, a modern attempt to sound like a Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 如果你在BBC网站上搜索，你会发现一个非常有趣的重建，那是现代人试图模仿尼安德特人声音的尝试。

sentences.en: It won't be as amusing as this one.
sentences.zh: 那肯定没有这个有趣。

sentences.en: So it's very amusing, and perhaps Tom should view that before he does his reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常有趣，也许汤姆在做他的重建之前应该看看那个。

sentences.en: I might just do that.
sentences.zh: 我可能会那样做。

sentences.en: But it's very funny.
sentences.zh: 但这非常滑稽。

sentences.en: I recommend you find it and have a laugh.
sentences.zh: 我建议你找到它并笑一笑。

sentences.en: But in reality, yes, of course, they may have been slightly different in sound.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，是的，当然，他们的声音可能略有不同。

sentences.en: We can tell from the ear bones actually are preserved of Neanderthals to compare with modern humans, and they are slightly differently shaped to our own ear bones.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上可以通过尼安德特人保存下来的耳骨与现代人类进行比较，它们的形状与我们自己的耳骨略有不同。

sentences.en: But when you test the acoustic properties of the Neanderthal hearing system as much as we can reconstruct it, it seems to be similar to our own in its range of hearing.
sentences.zh: 但是当你测试尼安德特人听觉系统的声学特性时，就我们所能重建的程度来看，它在听觉范围上似乎与我们自己的相似。

sentences.en: So at least from that point of view, similar.
sentences.zh: 所以至少从那个角度来看，是相似的。

sentences.en: And some people think that the Neanderthal vocal tract would not have been as versatile as ours.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为尼安德特人的声道不会像我们那样灵活。

sentences.en: It couldn't produce as many sounds.
sentences.zh: 它无法发出那么多种声音。

sentences.en: That's a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可能性。

sentences.en: But of course, there was a really, let's say, extreme reconstruction of Neanderthals that suggested they only had 20% of the vocal repertoire of sounds that we could make.
sentences.zh: 但当然，曾经有一个非常，怎么说呢，极端的尼安德特人重建，认为他们只能发出我们能发出的声音库中20%的声音。

sentences.en: But as someone pointed out at the time, there are many modern human languages that only make 20% of the sounds you could make.
sentences.zh: 但正如当时有人指出的那样，许多现代人类语言也只使用你能发出的声音中的20%。

sentences.en: So on its own, that wouldn't limit the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 所以仅凭这一点，并不会限制尼安德特人。

sentences.en: Language is a product of the brain, and language evolves out of social complexity.
sentences.zh: 语言是大脑的产物，语言是从社会复杂性中演化出来的。

sentences.en: So for me, we know from their archaeology that the Neanderthals led complex lives.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，我们从他们的考古学中知道，尼安德特人过着复杂的生活。

sentences.en: And I think that that signifies they would have had some form of speech and language.
sentences.zh: 我认为这表明他们会有某种形式的言语和语言。

sentences.en: And it may not have been as complex as the language we're using now.
sentences.zh: 它可能不像我们现在使用的语言那么复杂。

sentences.en: Perhaps their language did not have concepts of deep time.
sentences.zh: 也许他们的语言没有深层时间的概念。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: Abstraction, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 抽象概念，我们不知道。

sentences.en: But certainly in practical terms, I think the Neanderthals must have had language.
sentences.zh: 但肯定在实际层面上，我认为尼安德特人一定拥有语言。

sentences.en: They're leading complex lives.
sentences.zh: 他们过着复杂的生活。

sentences.en: They're surviving under difficult conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们在困难的条件下生存。

sentences.en: They're hunting difficult animals.
sentences.zh: 他们在猎杀难以对付的动物。

sentences.en: They're moving over the landscape in complex ways and living in relatively large groups.
sentences.zh: 他们以复杂的方式在景观中移动，并生活在相对较大的群体中。

sentences.en: So I think I would certainly give them a language capability.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我肯定会赋予他们语言能力。

sentences.en: So the idea that they have very high-pitched voices seems counterintuitive because physically they're larger than humans, are they?
sentences.zh: 所以他们有很高音调的声音这一想法似乎违反直觉，因为从生理上讲，他们比人类大，是吗？

sentences.en: They kind of have to eat more.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎需要吃得更多。

sentences.en: The energy demands on them are greater.
sentences.zh: 他们对能量的需求更大。

sentences.en: Obviously, we've got to remember that modern humans around the world vary greatly in size and shape.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们必须记住，世界各地的现代人类在体型和形状上差异很大。

sentences.en: So it depends who we're comparing them with.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于我们是在和谁比较。

sentences.en: But yes, compared with, let's say, the average European, Neanderthals were shorter and wider.
sentences.zh: 但确实，与，比方说，普通欧洲人相比，尼安德特人更矮、更宽。

sentences.en: And they were heavily bodied.
sentences.zh: 而且他们身体强壮。

sentences.en: So they were very muscular and very powerfully built, very powerful upper body.
sentences.zh: 所以他们肌肉非常发达，体格非常强健，上半身非常有力。

sentences.en: You probably wouldn't want to get in a wrestling match with a Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想和尼安德特人进行摔跤比赛。

sentences.en: So they're more like me than like Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以他们更像我，而不是像汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't want to have stereotypes, but maybe, maybe.
sentences.zh: 我不想有刻板印象，但也许，也许吧。

sentences.en: Do that DNA test, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 去做那个DNA测试吧，多米尼克。

sentences.en: We don't know how much hair they had, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他们有多少毛发，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's a bit worrying.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人担忧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Even body hair.
sentences.zh: 甚至是体毛。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: Obviously, the reconstructions of Neanderthals through time, if we look at them, we can see this pendulum swinging of making them look very human or very subhuman.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果我们回顾尼安德特人随时间推移的重建，我们可以看到这种钟摆式的摇摆，让他们看起来非常像人或者非常像亚人类。

sentences.en: And now the reconstructions in museums, including our own in London, show them as very human and relatively hairless.
sentences.zh: 而现在博物馆里的重建，包括我们伦敦博物馆里的，显示他们非常像人，而且相对没有毛发。

sentences.en: But of course, we don't actually know how much body hair they had.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们实际上并不知道他们有多少体毛。

sentences.en: And it probably varied through time.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能随时间而变化。

sentences.en: At times, they lived in very cold conditions and a short and wide body would be a good body shape to have because you're minimizing your surface area to save heat.
sentences.zh: 有时他们生活在非常寒冷的条件下，矮而宽的身体会是一种很好的体型，因为你可以通过最小化表面积来保存热量。

sentences.en: They may have had layers of subcutaneous fat to help them in that adaptation.
sentences.zh: 他们可能拥有皮下脂肪层来帮助他们进行那种适应。

sentences.en: And I'm sure their culture, you know, they would have had some form of clothing.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信他们的文化，你知道，他们会有某种形式的衣服。

sentences.en: They would have had shelters, things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们会有住所，诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: But of course, most of the evidence of that has disappeared.
sentences.zh: 但当然，大部分证据都已经消失了。

sentences.en: But now and again, we do find very strange structures that were made by Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 但偶尔，我们确实会发现尼安德特人建造的非常奇怪的结构。

sentences.en: So there's a site in France called Bruniquel, a Bruniquel cave, one of many caves in that
sentences.zh: 所以法国有一个叫布吕尼凯（Bruniquel）的遗址，布吕尼凯洞穴，是众多洞穴中的一个

sentences.en: Bruniquel area.
sentences.zh: 布吕尼凯地区。

sentences.en: And one very deep cave has an astonishing discovery.
sentences.zh: 其中一个非常深的洞穴里有着惊人的发现。

sentences.en: So deep in the cave, hundreds of meters in the dark zone of that cave, archaeologists have recovered a couple of stone structures deep in this cave.
sentences.zh: 在洞穴深处，也就是黑暗区域几百米远的地方，考古学家发现了几处石质结构。

sentences.en: They're basically elliptical structures, which are basically dry stone walls made out of stalagmites.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上是椭圆形的结构，是由石笋堆砌而成的干石墙。

sentences.en: So the Neanderthals went deep into this cave, way beyond the daylight zone.
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人曾深入这个洞穴，远超出了日光照射的范围。

sentences.en: They must have had fire to do that lighting.
sentences.zh: 他们当时一定有火来照明。

sentences.en: And they took stalagmites, broke them up and built like dry stone walls to make these elliptical structures.
sentences.zh: 他们取来石笋，将其敲碎，像堆砌干石墙一样建造了这些椭圆形结构。

sentences.en: There are at least two of them.
sentences.zh: 至少有两处这样的结构。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's that's all we've got at the moment of these strange structures deep in the cave.
sentences.zh: 目前关于这些洞穴深处的奇异结构，我们所知仅限于此。

sentences.en: Why were they there?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会在那里？

sentences.en: Was this some kind of ritual behavior?
sentences.zh: 这是一种某种仪式行为吗？

sentences.en: Were they living down in the cave?
sentences.zh: 他们当时住在洞穴里吗？

sentences.en: The area has yet to be excavated systematically.
sentences.zh: 该区域尚未进行系统性的发掘。

sentences.en: So we don't really know what there are signs of bones that have been burned.
sentences.zh: 所以我们并不真正清楚那里是否有骨头被焚烧的迹象。

sentences.en: So some animal bones are high in fat and they can actually be burnt for light.
sentences.zh: 有些动物骨头脂肪含量很高，实际上可以用来燃烧照明。

sentences.en: And so actually they were burning pieces of bone at this site to provide light.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上他们是在这个遗址焚烧骨头碎片来提供光源。

sentences.en: It's possible this was I mean, this was during a cold phase about 175,000 years ago, and maybe the cave actually was relatively warmer.
sentences.zh: 这也有可能——我的意思是，这发生在大约175,000年前的寒冷时期，也许洞穴里相对温暖一些。

sentences.en: We know that a river actually went through the cave.
sentences.zh: 我们知道确实有一条河流穿过了这个洞穴。

sentences.en: So it came from the surface through the cave and then out again to the surface.
sentences.zh: 它从地表流入洞穴，然后又流回地表。

sentences.en: So it's possible the Neanderthals were tracking that river in going down into the cave.
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人有可能是沿着那条河进入洞穴的。

sentences.en: But why they would have set up this camp, if that's what it is, deep in the cave like that,
sentences.zh: 但如果这确实是个营地，他们为什么要把它设在洞穴那么深的地方，

sentences.en: is a question we simply cannot answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们根本无法回答的问题。

sentences.en: And some people think it signifies some ritual behavior.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为这象征着某种仪式行为。

sentences.en: I think it might be a more practical thing that they were actually living down there.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能更实际一些，他们当时确实住在那里。

sentences.en: But we simply don't know.
sentences.zh: 但我们实在不得而知。

sentences.en: But it shows the complexity of their behavior.
sentences.zh: 但这显示了他们行为的复杂性。

sentences.en: Because it could be the much later cave art or something.
sentences.zh: 因为这可能是更晚期的洞穴艺术之类的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, kind of monumental or some temple or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，某种纪念碑、神庙之类的建筑。

sentences.en: Is that going too far?
sentences.zh: 这是否有点言过其实了？

sentences.en: Well, you know, archaeologists, you know, the joke is that, you know, when an archaeologist can't explain something, they say it's a richer object.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，考古学界有个笑话，当考古学家无法解释某样东西时，他们就会说那是某种仪式用品。

sentences.en: And that's what we're up against here with this structure.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们面对这个结构时所处的困境。

sentences.en: We simply don't know what it is and when it can be excavated systematically.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道它是什么，也不知道何时能进行系统性发掘。

sentences.en: So what we don't know is what's actually on the floor of these structures.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道这些结构的地板上到底有什么。

sentences.en: It hasn't been excavated yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有发掘过。

sentences.en: So if there are stone tools and butchered animal bones, then obviously they were living there.
sentences.zh: 如果那里有石器和被屠宰的动物骨头，那么显然他们曾住在那里。

sentences.en: But if there aren't any of those things, then that might promote the belief that this is some kind of a special ritual structure.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有这些东西，那可能会加强这是一种特殊仪式结构的观点。

sentences.en: And you mentioned cave art.
sentences.zh: 你提到了洞穴艺术。

sentences.en: And of course, that's that's one of the things that more than 20 years ago was supposed to separate us from the Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 当然，那也是20多年前被认为将我们与尼安德特人区分开来的特征之一。

sentences.en: So in Africa, we were developing symbolic expression.
sentences.zh: 在非洲，我们当时正在发展象征性表达。

sentences.en: We were using red ochre and we were engraving.
sentences.zh: 我们使用红赭石并进行雕刻。

sentences.en: And when we came out of Africa, we started to paint caves and these beautiful cave paintings of animals that we find in many caves.
sentences.zh: 当我们走出非洲后，我们开始绘制洞穴，也就是我们在许多洞穴中发现的那些美丽的动物壁画。

sentences.en: Apparently, that was something the Neanderthals simply couldn't do.
sentences.zh: 显然，那是尼安德特人根本做不到的事情。

sentences.en: But we now know that there are many sites where there's lots of ochre, red ochre and dark pigments collected by Neanderthals in really large quantities.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在知道，有许多遗址中发现了大量由尼安德特人收集的赭石、红赭石和深色颜料。

sentences.en: Now, some of it, you know, you can use ochre for practical purposes, apparently softening skins, apparently rubbing on the skin as an insecticide, things like that.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一些赭石可能用于实际目的，比如软化兽皮，或者涂抹在皮肤上作为杀虫剂之类的。

sentences.en: But there's so much of it that it looks like it was being used for marking bodies and potentially marking cave walls.
sentences.zh: 但数量实在太多了，看起来像是被用来标记身体，甚至可能用来标记洞穴墙壁。

sentences.en: And now from Spain, there are sites dating from more than 60,000 years ago, which have markings on the walls that seem to be made by Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 现在在西班牙，有一些距今6万多年前的遗址，墙壁上的标记似乎就是尼安德特人留下的。

sentences.en: It is controversial.
sentences.zh: 这很有争议。

sentences.en: There are some people who challenge the dating.
sentences.zh: 有些人对测年结果提出了质疑。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think it's quite likely with all that pigment around that Neanderthals were marking their bodies.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，考虑到周围有那么多颜料，尼安德特人很可能是在标记自己的身体。

sentences.en: And we know that Neanderthals made pendants.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道尼安德特人制作吊坠。

sentences.en: They made jewelry.
sentences.zh: 他们制作珠宝。

sentences.en: You know, we have examples of pierced animal teeth from Neanderthal sites.
sentences.zh: 我们有在尼安德特人遗址发现的带孔动物牙齿的例子。

sentences.en: We have shells with holes in that look like they've been suspended and even colored with ochre.
sentences.zh: 我们有带孔的贝壳，看起来像是被悬挂过，甚至还涂上了赭石。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are even talons of birds of prey that look like they've been suspended.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有猛禽的爪子，看起来也像是被悬挂过。

sentences.en: As jewelry or pendants.
sentences.zh: 作为珠宝或吊坠。

sentences.en: So the Neanderthals had that.
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人拥有这些。

sentences.en: They were signaling to each other in a way that we would see as very, very human.
sentences.zh: 他们以一种我们认为非常、非常人性化的方式相互传递信号。

sentences.en: And Chris, what about burials?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，那埋葬习俗呢？

sentences.en: So the idea in the 60s that they were buried with flowers is not thought to be true anymore.
sentences.zh: 60年代那种他们用花朵陪葬的说法，现在已经不再被认为是真实的了。

sentences.en: But there is evidence that they had some sense, perhaps, of an afterlife, that they weren't just kind of leaving bodies to rot.
sentences.zh: 但有证据表明他们或许有某种来世观念，他们并非只是任由尸体腐烂。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, for me, there is enough, more than enough evidence that Neanderthals were burying their dead.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，对我来说，有足够多、甚至绰绰有余的证据表明尼安德特人会埋葬死者。

sentences.en: The fact that we've got so many Neanderthal skeletons, some people have challenged that these were intentional burials,
sentences.zh: 虽然我们发现了这么多尼安德特人骨架，但有些人质疑这些是否是有意的埋葬，

sentences.en: that these were individuals whose body just washed into a crevice in a cave, or it was a rock fall and the Neanderthal was buried under a load of rocks.
sentences.zh: 认为这些个体可能只是尸体被冲进了洞穴裂缝，或者是岩石坍塌导致尼安德特人被埋在岩石堆下。

sentences.en: That could certainly have happened.
sentences.zh: 这种情况当然可能发生。

sentences.en: But I think there are enough examples now that we can say that Neanderthals intentionally buried their dead.
sentences.zh: 但我认为现在有足够的例子让我们断定尼安德特人是有意埋葬死者的。

sentences.en: And not just adults.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是成年人。

sentences.en: These are burials of children as well.
sentences.zh: 也有儿童的墓葬。

sentences.en: So, yes, I think they buried their dead.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为他们会埋葬死者。

sentences.en: Now, of course, interpreting why they did it is another issue.
sentences.zh: 当然，解读他们为什么要这样做是另一个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, another matter.
sentences.zh: 没错，那是另一回事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Was it, you know, did it start off as hygienic, maybe, that they didn't want to leave a body out on the surface to attract hyenas and dangerous other predators?
sentences.zh: 这是否最初出于卫生考虑？也许他们不想把尸体留在地表吸引鬣狗和其他危险的捕食者？

sentences.en: So the bodies were covered up just to get them out of the way.
sentences.zh: 所以把尸体掩埋只是为了处理掉它们。

sentences.en: Perhaps it could be an extension of care because one of the individuals from Shanidar, Shanidar 1, the first one that was discovered, was probably a burial.
sentences.zh: 也许这可能是关怀的延伸，因为沙尼达尔遗址的其中一个个体，即沙尼达尔1号，也就是第一个被发现的那个，很可能就是一次埋葬。

sentences.en: That individual was severely disabled for the last at least probably 10 years of his life.
sentences.zh: 那个个体在他生命的最后至少10年里严重残疾。

sentences.en: So that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He was a cripple, possibly blind in one eye.
sentences.zh: 他是个瘸子，可能还有一只眼睛失明。

sentences.en: And so it seems very likely people were provisioning for him.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来很可能有人在供养他。

sentences.en: And maybe the burial of that individual is caring for the body after death.
sentences.zh: 也许对那个个体的埋葬就是死后的关怀。

sentences.en: So you've invested this care in that person during their life and you invest care when they die as well.
sentences.zh: 你在他生前投入了这种关怀，在他死后也同样投入了关怀。

sentences.en: Whether there's a concept of an afterlife, maybe that is an add on at a later stage.
sentences.zh: 至于是否存在来世的概念，也许那是后期才有的附加内容。

sentences.en: But who knows?
sentences.zh: 但谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Neanderthals could have had that concept too.
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人也可能拥有那种概念。

sentences.en: Well, Chris, so is there any sense that, I mean, if we look at Homo sapiens, history in a sense,
sentences.zh: 那么克里斯，如果我们审视智人的历史，在某种意义上，

sentences.en: I mean, we can cast it as a tale of progress, and I use the word very advisedly, but technological advances leading to ever more complicated societies.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将其描述为一个进步的故事——我使用这个词是非常谨慎的——即技术进步导致了日益复杂的社会。

sentences.en: Do we have any sense of that happening with the Neanderthals?
sentences.zh: 我们有任何迹象表明尼安德特人也发生了这种情况吗？

sentences.en: Is there a sense that their society is becoming more technologically advanced?
sentences.zh: 是否有迹象表明他们的社会在变得更加技术先进？

sentences.en: Are they differing, evolving, changing over time?
sentences.zh: 他们是否在随着时间推移而产生差异、进化或改变？

sentences.en: Well, I think they must have been.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们一定会的。

sentences.en: There's certainly a significant change of behavior that we see both in Neanderthals and modern human evolution,
sentences.zh: 我们在尼安德特人和现代人类进化中确实看到了显著的行为变化，

sentences.en: where the earliest examples of probably the Neanderthal lineage and the sapiens lineage are associated with stone tools that we call hand axes.
sentences.zh: 最早的尼安德特人谱系和智人谱系的例子都与我们称为手斧的石器有关。

sentences.en: So these are almond-shaped, often pointed, bifacially worked tools.
sentences.zh: 这些是杏仁状、通常带有尖头、双面加工的工具。

sentences.en: They sit in the hand nicely, and we call them hand axes.
sentences.zh: 它们握在手里很顺手，我们称之为手斧。

sentences.en: We don't know what the people at the time called them, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们不知道当时的人们怎么称呼它们。

sentences.en: So these hand axes were associated with early Neanderthals and with early Homo sapiens in Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以这些手斧与早期的尼安德特人和非洲的早期智人有关。

sentences.en: But about 300,000 years ago, there's a switch in behavior, and we start to see the appearance of what are called prepared core tools, sometimes called lavalua tools.
sentences.zh: 但在大约30万年前，行为发生了转变，我们开始看到所谓的预制石核工具的出现，有时被称为勒瓦娄哇工具。

sentences.en: And there, the shape of the artifact is predetermined.
sentences.zh: 在那里，制品的形状是预先确定的。

sentences.en: You map out in the core the shape you want your flake to be, and then you strike it off with a single blow, and you have a predetermined shape of tool.
sentences.zh: 你在石核上规划好你想要的石片形状，然后用一击将其敲下，你就得到了预定形状的工具。

sentences.en: So this technology spreads across much of the Neanderthal and early Homo sapiens world, and that's then the dominant technology for the next 200,000 years.
sentences.zh: 这种技术传播到了尼安德特人和早期智人的大部分世界，并成为随后20万年里的主流技术。

sentences.en: So there is that change that goes on in both Neanderthals and early Homo sapiens.
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人和早期智人确实都发生了那种变化。

sentences.en: And even within that, you do see many different tool types.
sentences.zh: 即便在那个范围内，你也能看到许多不同的工具类型。

sentences.en: So within Neanderthals, we see them capable of producing tools that would have been good for working skins.
sentences.zh: 在尼安德特人中，我们看到他们有能力制造适合处理兽皮的工具。

sentences.en: So they're wearing clothes?
sentences.zh: 所以他们穿衣服吗？

sentences.en: We assume so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们假设是这样，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, again, the evidence is, you know, there's no direct evidence for that, really.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，同样，证据是……你知道，真的没有直接证据。

sentences.en: But the fact they've got this technology, which, and we know that the tools themselves show wear on them.
sentences.zh: 但他们拥有这种技术，而且我们知道工具本身显示出磨损痕迹。

sentences.en: Sometimes there are bone tools that have been used to, which today would be used to rub skins, and they show a polish on the end.
sentences.zh: 有时会有骨制工具，在今天会被用来揉搓兽皮，它们的末端显示出抛光痕迹。

sentences.en: So those tools are known from Neanderthal sites.
sentences.zh: 所以这些工具在尼安德特人遗址中是已知的。

sentences.en: So Neanderthals were pretty certainly working skins for clothing.
sentences.zh: 因此，尼安德特人几乎可以肯定是在加工兽皮以制作衣服。

sentences.en: I mean, they're living in, at times, very severe winters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们有时生活在非常严酷的冬天里。

sentences.en: So we assume they must have had some form of clothing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们假设他们一定有某种形式的服装。

sentences.en: Chris, what about their social structure?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，那他们的社会结构呢？

sentences.en: Do they have, because you've alluded a few times to their social structure, but are they in, you're saying they're in big groups,
sentences.zh: 因为你已经几次提到他们的社会结构了，但他们是……你是说他们处于大群体中，

sentences.en: but do we have any sense of, are they big enough groups to be like a clan or a tribe or an extended family, or what do we think they are?
sentences.zh: 但我们有任何概念吗，他们是像氏族、部落或大家庭那样的大群体，还是我们认为他们是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, we can't really say about numbers in total.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们无法真正说明总人数。

sentences.en: I mean, people have reconstructed that groups within caves, when you look at flint scatters and sizes of habitation, that Neanderthals could be in groups of 20 or 30.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们通过观察燧石散布情况和居住规模，推测尼安德特人可能以20到30人的群体生活。

sentences.en: But whether they were in much bigger aggregations at times, we simply don't know.
sentences.zh: 但他们是否有时会聚集成更大的群体，我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: As I mentioned already, probably towards the end of their time, there's genetic evidence that the Neanderthals were relatively low in variation,
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，可能在他们时代的末期，有遗传证据表明尼安德特人的变异性相对较低，

sentences.en: and there's some evidence of inbreeding.
sentences.zh: 并且有一些近亲繁殖的证据。

sentences.en: In some Neanderthal sites, we see from the DNA that individuals are closely related,
sentences.zh: 在一些尼安德特人遗址中，我们从DNA中看到个体之间关系密切，

sentences.en: and there's a site in Spain where you have quite a few anomalies in the skeletons of the Neanderthals from that site that suggests that they could have been inbreeding,
sentences.zh: 西班牙有一个遗址，那里的尼安德特人骨架中有相当多的异常情况，这表明他们可能存在近亲繁殖，

sentences.en: and therefore, you know, that's not good for the genetic health of the population.
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道，这对种群的遗传健康是不利的。

sentences.en: So, at times, the Neanderthals were challenged, and there's the tricky matter of cannibalism.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时尼安德特人面临挑战，还有一个棘手的食人问题。

sentences.en: We haven't come on to that one yet, but we know that both Neanderthals and modern humans have indulged in cannibalism,
sentences.zh: 我们还没谈到那个，但我们知道尼安德特人和现代人类都曾有过食人行为，

sentences.en: and we see this in a number of Neanderthal sites where you find human remains of Neanderthals with cut marks on them.
sentences.zh: 我们在许多尼安德特人遗址中都看到了这一点，那里发现了带有切割痕迹的尼安德特人遗骸。

sentences.en: So, these individuals have been defleshed,
sentences.zh: 所以，这些个体被剔除了肉，

sentences.en: and so is that for consumption?
sentences.zh: 那么这是为了食用吗？

sentences.en: Is it some kind of ritual behaviour, ritual treatment of the dead?
sentences.zh: 这是某种仪式行为，对死者的仪式性处理吗？

sentences.en: So, are they eating their enemies, or is it more a tribute to the dead?
sentences.zh: 所以，他们是在吃掉敌人，还是这更多是对死者的致敬？

sentences.en: And those are both possibilities.
sentences.zh: 这两种可能性都存在。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing about that is that it, again, it's like a kind of Rorschach teSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于这一点，它再次像是一种罗夏墨迹测试。

sentences.en: Do you think that humans are naturally savage and violent, or do you think that they care for the dead and whatever?
sentences.zh: 你认为人类天生野蛮暴力，还是认为他们关心死者等等？

sentences.en: Or maybe it's both, a bit of both.
sentences.zh: 或者也许两者皆有，各占一部分。

sentences.en: But, I mean, it is a kind of philosophical divide, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这是一种哲学上的分歧，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I simply don't know the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我根本不知道答案。

sentences.en: And certainly, if you speak to an archaeologist, you know, you will get both sides of the story there, that there is a view that one reason why we survived
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你和考古学家交谈，你会听到故事的两个方面，有一种观点认为我们之所以幸存下来，

sentences.en: is that we were less aggressive within our groups, that we were friendlier.
sentences.zh: 是因为我们在群体内部不那么好斗，我们更友好。

sentences.en: Survival of the friendlies that modern humans...
sentences.zh: 适者生存，即最友好的人生存，现代人类……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I find that very counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常反直觉。

sentences.en: Within our groups.
sentences.zh: 在我们的群体内部。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Within our groups, I say.
sentences.zh: 我说的是在我们的群体内部。

sentences.en: Of course, outside your group is a different story, apparently.
sentences.zh: 当然，群体之外的情况显然是另一回事。

sentences.en: And so modern humans were able to build larger numbers of people with friendly relations within that group, a reduction of aggression.
sentences.zh: 所以现代人类能够建立起人数更多、群体内部关系友好的社会，减少了攻击性。

sentences.en: And the Neanderthals and these other humans had lower, at higher levels of interpersonal aggression.
sentences.zh: 而尼安德特人和其他人类则有更高水平的人际攻击性。

sentences.en: And we managed to reduce that, and that was part of the reason for our success.
sentences.zh: 我们设法减少了这一点，这就是我们成功的部分原因。

sentences.en: Now, these are just, obviously, ideas, and I'm not capable or even competent to judge whether those ideas are correct.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些仅仅是想法，我既没有能力也没有资格去评判这些想法是否正确。

sentences.en: But it's certainly one possibility.
sentences.zh: 但这无疑是一种可能性。

sentences.en: That's fascinating, though, because it challenges the idea that is so common in popular culture, that humanity, that Homo sapiens succeeded because of our unpleasantness.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思，因为它挑战了流行文化中一个非常普遍的观点，即人类，也就是智人，之所以成功是因为我们的卑劣。

sentences.en: You know, that we were more cunning and more cruel and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是说我们更狡猾、更残忍，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's back to the inheritor's image, of course, that, you know, we basically killed off the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这又回到了继承者的形象，当然，你知道，我们基本上消灭了尼安德特人。

sentences.en: And there is a view around that, yeah, we kind of killed them off in some long-term warfare.
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为，是的，我们在某种长期的战争中消灭了他们。

sentences.en: But the coexistence in Europe and Asia from 60,000 to 40,000, that's at least 20,000 years of some kind of coexistence of the two groups,
sentences.zh: 但在欧洲和亚洲从6万年前到4万年前的共存期，那至少有2万年的时间里，这两个群体以某种方式共存着，

sentences.en: including what we now know are multiple examples of interbreeding between the two groups.
sentences.zh: 包括我们现在所知的这两个群体之间多次杂交的例子。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's certainly not, you know, instantaneous aggression and warfare.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这肯定不是那种瞬间发生的侵略和战争。

sentences.en: And, you know, I often think that, you know, the extinction of the Neanderthals was kind of a – it could even be accidental.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我经常认为，尼安德特人的灭绝可能是一种——甚至可能是偶然的。

sentences.en: It wasn't intentional.
sentences.zh: 那不是故意的。

sentences.en: So, you know, orangutans in Southeast Asia are going extinct, not because people want them to go extinct, but, you know, we're removing their food,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，东南亚的红毛猩猩正在灭绝，不是因为人们想让它们灭绝，而是因为，你知道，我们正在移除它们的食物，

sentences.en: we're removing their living sites, we're removing their environments.
sentences.zh: 我们正在移除它们的栖息地，我们正在移除它们的环境。

sentences.en: And they are going extinct.
sentences.zh: 它们正在灭绝。

sentences.en: We didn't intend it, but it happens.
sentences.zh: 我们并非有意为之，但事情就这样发生了。

sentences.en: And that's what's happened to so many species probably around the world.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是世界上许多物种所经历的情况。

sentences.en: I'm sure when people arrived in New Zealand, their first intention wasn't to kill off all the large native birds, but that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 我相信当人们到达新西兰时，他们的初衷并不是要杀光所有大型原生鸟类，但事情就是这样发生了。

sentences.en: And so the extinction of the Neanderthals, at least the physical extinction, and I stress not the genetic extinction, the physical extinction of the Neanderthals,
sentences.zh: 所以尼安德特人的灭绝，至少是物理上的灭绝，我强调不是基因上的灭绝，尼安德特人的物理灭绝，

sentences.en: could have been not intentional.
sentences.zh: 可能并非出于故意。

sentences.en: Modern humans weren't going out to do them in and finish them off, but by taking prime age individuals out of their breeding pool, by hunting the same animals,
sentences.zh: 现代人类并不是要出去把他们干掉并彻底消灭他们，而是通过从他们的繁殖库中带走壮年个体，通过猎杀同样的动物，

sentences.en: by collecting the same plant resources, by wanting to live in the best cave sites,
sentences.zh: 通过采集同样的植物资源，通过想要住在最好的洞穴里，

sentences.en: automatically they were doing that to the detriment of the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 自动地，我们就在损害尼安德特人的利益。

sentences.en: Maybe we impacted on Neanderthals in the way that we impacted on megafauna across the world, that we may not even deliberately have hunted them or anything, but that we juSt...
sentences.zh: 也许我们对尼安德特人的影响就像我们对世界各地巨型动物群的影响一样，我们甚至可能没有刻意去猎杀它们，但我们只是……

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Do you think that's the likeliest explanation?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是最可能的解释吗？

sentences.en: I mean, there are claims that there are a couple of examples of interpersonal violence that could be between a Neanderthal and a Sapiens, but I don't think those are sure for me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有人声称有几个尼安德特人和智人之间发生人际暴力的例子，但我认为这些对我来说并不确定。

sentences.en: They could equally be Neanderthals that are...
sentences.zh: 它们同样可能是尼安德特人……

sentences.en: You know, there's one of the Shanidar Neanderthals has a wound on one of his ribs that's partly healed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，沙尼达尔尼安德特人中有一个人的肋骨上有一处部分愈合的伤口。

sentences.en: Because they had spears, right?
sentences.zh: 因为他们有长矛，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, they had spears.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们有长矛。

sentences.en: So, you know, someone said, well, maybe that's a modern human doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以，有人说，嗯，也许那是现代人类干的。

sentences.en: Well, we have no idea.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: And equally, it could have been a Neanderthal doing it.
sentences.zh: 同样，也可能是尼安德特人干的。

sentences.en: It could have even been a hunting accident.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是一次狩猎事故。

sentences.en: You know, we can't be sure of the cause there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们无法确定那里的原因。

sentences.en: So what we can say is that we're beginning to find increasing evidence of these groups in close proximity.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以说的是，我们开始发现越来越多的证据表明这些群体曾经近距离接触。

sentences.en: We don't have the dating precision to say that they're actually there at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我们没有精确的年代测定来证明他们确实在同一时间出现在那里。

sentences.en: But the fact the interbreeding happened on multiple occasions means those populations must have been in close proximity.
sentences.zh: 但杂交多次发生的事实意味着这些种群一定曾经近距离接触过。

sentences.en: And partners are moving for whatever reason between one group and the other.
sentences.zh: 而且伴侣们出于某种原因在两个群体之间流动。

sentences.en: And those children, those hybrid children, they're being brought up within a modern human group.
sentences.zh: 而那些孩子，那些混血儿，是在现代人类群体中长大的。

sentences.en: And they're continuing, you know, in that group and they're breeding on in that group.
sentences.zh: 他们继续留在那个群体中，并在那个群体中繁衍。

sentences.en: Just a question.
sentences.zh: 只是一个问题。

sentences.en: I think we're very close to the end now, aren't we, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在快结束了，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: But just a question about the afterlife of the Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 只是关于尼安德特人来世的一个问题。

sentences.en: So two of our listeners sent in questions about whether they live on in myths and legends,
sentences.zh: 我们的两位听众发来了关于他们是否活在神话和传说中的问题，

sentences.en: Stefan Jensen and Meta-Burbia, whether after the Neanderthals sort of physically vanished from the scene, whether they lived on as giants, trolls, orcs,
sentences.zh: 斯特凡·詹森和梅塔·伯比亚，在尼安德特人从现场物理消失后，他们是否作为巨人、巨魔、兽人活了下来，

sentences.en: all these things which are there in almost all myths and kind of folkloric stories.
sentences.zh: 所有这些几乎存在于所有神话和民间故事中的东西。

sentences.en: Do you think there could be some kind of vestige of a time when we walk the earth together?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是否可能是我们共同行走在地球上的那个时代的某种遗迹？

sentences.en: A Jungian memory.
sentences.zh: 一种荣格式的记忆。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's obviously going to have to be very deep time because we're talking 40,000 years.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这显然必须是非常久远的时间，因为我们谈论的是4万年前。

sentences.en: And for me, that's a difficult thing to establish.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一件很难确定的事情。

sentences.en: But Bjorn Katen, a paleontologist, he wrote a series of novels also about the Neanderthal-modern human interface and interaction.
sentences.zh: 但是古生物学家比约恩·卡滕写了一系列关于尼安德特人与现代人类界面和互动的小说。

sentences.en: And they are really good as well.
sentences.zh: 它们也非常棒。

sentences.en: And I recommend them.
sentences.zh: 我推荐它们。

sentences.en: One called Dance of the Tiger.
sentences.zh: 其中一本叫《虎之舞》。

sentences.en: And in there, the modern humans call the Neanderthals trolls.
sentences.zh: 在书中，现代人类称尼安德特人为巨魔。

sentences.en: That is their name for them.
sentences.zh: 那是他们对他们的称呼。

sentences.en: So, you know, there is that implication there that this particularly Katen was from Scandinavia.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这其中有一种暗示，尤其是卡滕来自斯堪的纳维亚。

sentences.en: So that's where that legend, those legends are very strong.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那些传说非常强烈的地方。

sentences.en: It would be odd if there weren't a kind of buried memory somewhere deep within us that there were once,
sentences.zh: 如果我们的内心深处没有一种埋藏的记忆，即曾经有，

sentences.en: you know, other creatures who were like us, but were not us, if you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其他像我们但又不是我们的生物，如果我没说错的话，那才奇怪。

sentences.en: Do you not think?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: It's a long time.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: And the same applies over in Flores.
sentences.zh: 同样的情况也适用于弗洛勒斯岛。

sentences.en: So in Flores, we've got this weird creature nicknamed the Hobbit, Homo floresiensis.
sentences.zh: 在弗洛勒斯岛，我们有一种绰号为“霍比特人”的奇怪生物，即弗洛勒斯人。

sentences.en: And it was around until probably around 50,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它大约一直存在到5万年前。

sentences.en: And there are folk tales of strange little creatures living in the woods in Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 在东南亚，有关于森林里住着奇怪小生物的民间传说。

sentences.en: Are those some kind of memories from 40,000 years ago of the Hobbit?
sentences.zh: 那些是4万年前关于霍比特人的某种记忆吗？

sentences.en: Or are they actually referring to the orangutan or the gibbon or some other creatures that live in the woods?
sentences.zh: 还是它们实际上指的是红毛猩猩、长臂猿或其他生活在森林里的生物？

sentences.en: So I think those memories are certainly there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这些记忆肯定存在。

sentences.en: But for me, that's such deep time.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，那是太久远的时间了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't know that really there could be a survival like that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是否真的会有那样的幸存。

sentences.en: Chris, before we go, just one last question.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，在我们结束之前，最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Do you have any sense?
sentences.zh: 你有什么感觉吗？

sentences.en: Have people begun to think about whether in the wake of the pandemic, whether the Neanderthals might have been wiped out by some pandemic?
sentences.zh: 人们是否开始思考，在疫情之后，尼安德特人是否可能被某种流行病消灭了？

sentences.en: Perhaps this is something that is starting to surface in Neanderthal studies.
sentences.zh: 也许这是尼安德特人研究中开始浮现的东西。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that has come up that we had evolved in Africa.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实被提出来过，我们在非洲进化。

sentences.en: The Neanderthals had been evolving in Europe and Asia.
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人在欧洲和亚洲进化。

sentences.en: So we could have brought diseases from Africa that the Neanderthals had no immunity to.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能从非洲带来了尼安德特人没有免疫力的疾病。

sentences.en: And that's been proposed.
sentences.zh: 这已经被提出来了。

sentences.en: Certainly, there could have been those.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能发生过。

sentences.en: If the populations are in contact, then there could certainly be an exchange of pathogens and parasites between them.
sentences.zh: 如果种群之间有接触，那么它们之间肯定会有病原体和寄生虫的交换。

sentences.en: But, of course, many of the examples in recent history, for example, in South America,
sentences.zh: 但当然，近代史上的许多例子，例如在南美洲，

sentences.en: of where epidemics were carried from one population to another, those populations are living at quite high density.
sentences.zh: 流行病从一个种群传播到另一个种群，那些种群生活在相当高密度的地方。

sentences.en: And so there can be a rapid spread, as we have with COVID today.
sentences.zh: 所以可能会有迅速的传播，就像我们今天面对新冠病毒一样。

sentences.en: We're talking about much smaller groups spaced out on the landscape.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是在景观中分散开来的更小的群体。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure how much that could have run through a whole population and finished them off.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道这能在多大程度上贯穿整个种群并消灭他们。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is the inverse, that actually, obviously, having evolved in Africa, we didn't have any immunity to the diseases outside of Africa.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是反过来的情况，实际上，显然，由于在非洲进化，我们对非洲以外的疾病没有任何免疫力。

sentences.en: The Neanderthals, having evolved there, had evolved natural immunities to many of the local diseases.
sentences.zh: 尼安德特人在那里进化，对许多当地疾病进化出了天然免疫力。

sentences.en: And it seems likely that one of the advantages, if you like, of interbreeding with Neanderthals was we picked up some of their immune systeMs.
sentences.zh: 看起来很可能，如果你愿意的话，与尼安德特人杂交的优势之一就是我们获得了一些他们的免疫系统。

sentences.en: And so maybe that's why early waves of Homo sapiens failed to settle.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这就是为什么早期智人浪潮未能定居的原因。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, I mean, they may have just been too small in number and they couldn't cope with the climate changes any better than the Neanderthals could.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我的意思是，他们的人数可能太少了，他们无法比尼安德特人更好地应对气候变化。

sentences.en: And they just disappeared again.
sentences.zh: 他们就又消失了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I think that, you know, by interbreeding with Neanderthals, we got a quick fix to our immune systems outside of Africa.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我认为，你知道，通过与尼安德特人杂交，我们快速修复了我们在非洲以外的免疫系统。

sentences.en: And that helped us survive.
sentences.zh: 这帮助我们生存了下来。

sentences.en: Because it's still impacting on COVID, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为它仍然在影响新冠病毒，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's claimed that there are some variants which have derived from Neanderthals, which improve your resistance to COVID and others which act against it.
sentences.zh: 有人声称有一些变体源自尼安德特人，它们提高了你对新冠病毒的抵抗力，而另一些则起反作用。

sentences.en: And it's been even claimed that in different, because of course, Neanderthals DNA is spread right across.
sentences.zh: 甚至有人声称在不同的地方，因为当然，尼安德特人的DNA是广泛分布的。

sentences.en: Everyone outside of Africa has it in the Americas, in Australia, in Europe and so on.
sentences.zh: 非洲以外的每个人都有，在美洲、澳大利亚、欧洲等等。

sentences.en: So certainly those different variants could actually be helping or hindering the spread of COVID in modern human populations.
sentences.zh: 所以这些不同的变体确实可能正在帮助或阻碍新冠病毒在现代人类群体中的传播。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's quite possible.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这很有可能。

sentences.en: So, yes, the Neanderthals DNA is affecting our immune systems outside of Africa and still is today.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，尼安德特人的DNA正在影响我们在非洲以外的免疫系统，而且今天依然如此。

sentences.en: And it's possible that some autoimmune conditions are also linked with the presence of Neanderthal DNA.
sentences.zh: 而且某些自身免疫性疾病也可能与尼安德特人DNA的存在有关。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, our immune systems are too active and they even turn in on themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种意义上，我们的免疫系统太活跃了，甚至会攻击自身。

sentences.en: And that's also a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种可能性。

sentences.en: So they're not just prehistory.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不仅仅是史前历史。

sentences.en: I think that is absolutely the perfect note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是一个完美的结束语。

sentences.en: And, Chris, thanks so much for that.
sentences.zh: 而且，克里斯，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Can't thank you enough.
sentences.zh: 感激不尽。

sentences.zh: 汤姆，你想现在表演你的模仿秀吗？
